$comment: The hostile set, declared once and checked from both ends (item 38).
Two fixtures model this library and neither generates the other:
`gen-devdb` builds a real SQLite database the real engine reads, and
`gui/src/lib/api/fake.ts` is plain data for layers 1 and 2, which run in a
bare browser with no IPC and so cannot reach the first. That cost is paid on
purpose. What was not paid on purpose is the drift: `fake.ts` carried a
twenty-first case the database had no counterpart for, and the database's
covers had no counterpart in `fake.ts` at all.
So this file is the declaration and neither fixture is. Both are asserted
against it: `devdb.rs`'s `the_edge_cases_are_the_declared_ones`, and
`fake.test.ts`'s `the fake models exactly the declared edge cases`. Adding a
case to one fixture and not the other now fails on the side that was not
updated, which is the whole point — before this, it failed nowhere.
Hand-edited. Nothing generates it: a declaration generated from one of the
two things it governs would agree with that one no matter how wrong it was,
which is `crates/corpus`' own rule about oracles.
`id` is positional — both fixtures number the hostile set 1..=n in this
order, ahead of the two hundred ordinary books, so a reviewer meets the
cases and not the filler.
Fields are the intersection both fixtures can honestly answer. Highlights,
notes and tags are deliberately absent: they live in side tables in one and
in separate maps in the other, and a claim only one side can check is
decoration.

cases.title: A Book Of Zero Pages
cases.what: Item 17b's false denominator: a percentage over this is a divide by zero, and the honest answer is that there is no percentage.

cases.title: A Book Of Unknown Length
cases.what: Absence, not zero. A progress bar has nothing to draw and must not draw an empty one.

cases.title: The Doorstop
cases.what: The fat end of item 19's thickness scale, and the ordinary progress case.

cases.title: A Pamphlet
cases.what: The thin end of the same scale, where a spine has no room for a title.

cases.title: A Book With No Cover At All
cases.what: cover_path is NULL. Not a broken image and not an apology — the empty state has to be a designed one. The only declared case with no cover, which is what makes the cover-bearing rules assertable.

cases.title: A Title Of Such Considerable And Frankly Self-Indulgent Length That It Cannot Possibly Fit In A Shelf Tile Or A Column Header, Being In The Manner Of The Long Eighteenth Century, Wherein The Title Was Also The Blurb
cases.what: A 220-character title. Clipping, wrapping, and the tooltip that should carry the rest.

cases.title: A Book Filed Under Surname
cases.what: Author stored as `Surname, Given` — the calibre and Goodreads form. Whether it is displayed that way is item 17's, not a Svelte template's.

cases.title: A Book By One Name
cases.what: A mononym author. Any name-splitting rule breaks here.

cases.title: A Book By Nobody
cases.what: No author at all — a real state after a bare epub import, not an error to report.

cases.title: A Book By Three People
cases.what: Three authors. Where the join and the truncation happen.

cases.title: A Book I Put Down
cases.what: An abandoned reading. Never styled as a failure — decisions.md says so by name. Shaped identically to an open read, which is why the state had to cross the wire.

cases.title: A Book I Went Back To
cases.what: Two readings, one finished and one open. Item 28's card is per reading, so this book has two of them — and `reading_state` reports the open one.

cases.title: A Book I Finished
cases.what: A finished reading. Carries no page: every frontend that had this case dropped the numbers for a word.

cases.title: 北回帰線のあたりで
cases.what: CJK title and author. Font fallback, and character-count-based clipping being wrong.

cases.title: الكتاب الذي يقرأ من اليمين
cases.what: An RTL title. Bidi layout, and a left-aligned column that should not be.

cases.title: Ærøskøbing: Ångström's Œuvre — a Naïve Façade
cases.what: Diacritics and ligatures, including ones that break a naive sort.

An empty title — the schema's own default, reachable from a sidecar with no doc_props. It is the empty string and NOT null: `books.title` is `TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ''`, so a stored book's title is never null however Option-shaped the DTO is. `fake.ts` modelled null here until item 38, which is a state the database cannot produce.

cases.title: The Claw Of The Conciliator
cases.what: A series with an index. `series_index` is a REAL and prints as `#2`, never `#2.0`; the label is the engine's since item 17.

cases.title: A Book In A Series With No Number
cases.what: A series naming no index. The pair moves together or not at all, and nothing is invented to fill the gap.

cases.title: A Book With Subjects And Shelves
cases.what: Provider subjects beside minted shelves — two different things that look alike, and one of the separations migration 0013 rests on.

cases.title: A Book Some Other App Touched
cases.what: A reading whose status is a word this build does not know. `readings.status` has no CHECK constraint, so this is reachable rather than invented; the engine answers it with `ReadingState::Other { raw }` rather than failing to parse. `fake.ts` had this case and the database had no counterpart until item 38.
